# Trovarcis

> Trovarcis Sender is a Windows app for sending bulk email from your own email accounts (Gmail, Google Workspace, Zoho, Amazon SES, your own server or any other SMTP account). It costs $79 once, with no subscription. Your lists and your SMTP credentials are stored locally. Trovarcis never sees them. Alongside it, six web tools check your domain, list and message before you send. Three are free with no signup.

## Trovarcis Sender

- [Trovarcis Sender](https://trovarci.sh/sender): Bulk email software for Windows. Sends through SMTP accounts you already have, across several accounts at once. Before sending it checks the list and sets aside typos, duplicates and broken addresses. It keeps each account inside the daily and hourly limits you set and takes turns between accounts, pauses a campaign by itself if too many addresses are refused, never emails anyone on the Do not send list, and shows the mail server's own reason for every email that didn't arrive. $79 one payment, 3 computers, every 1.x update, 15-day refund. Buy today, get the Mac version free when it ships.
- [Pay with crypto](https://trovarci.sh/pay-with-crypto): How to pay with cryptocurrency.

## Tools

- [Domain Checker](https://trovarci.sh/domain): Checks whether a domain is set up so mail providers trust its email: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, mail servers, encryption, and blocklists (Spamhaus, SpamCop, Barracuda, PSBL, SURBL and the Spamhaus domain list). a plain fix for each problem. Free, no signup.
- [SMTP Tester](https://trovarci.sh/smtp-test): Tests an email account's server, port and password, and shows in plain words where a connection fails. Free, no signup.
- [DNS Record Generator](https://trovarci.sh/records): Writes the SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MX records for your domain and email provider, ready to copy into your DNS. Free, no signup.
- [Email Verifier](https://trovarci.sh/verify): Finds the addresses on a list that would bounce. One address or up to 50,000 per list. Results: valid, invalid, catch-all, disposable, role-based. 1 credit per address, and addresses that can't be billed are refunded.
- [Phone Number Checker](https://trovarci.sh/verify-number): Format check against each country's numbering plan, free. Carrier and line type (mobile, landline, VoIP, toll-free) for 2 credits per number, up to 10,000 per list. Landlines can't receive SMS.
- [Bulk email cost calculator](https://trovarci.sh/bulk-email-cost-calculator): Enter a list size and how often you send; see the monthly and three-year cost of Mailchimp Standard, Brevo, Amazon SES and Trovarcis Sender. Free, no signup. Results have their own URL, for example ?contacts=10000&sends=4.
- [Email Scorer](https://trovarci.sh/score): Scores an email out of 100 on subject line, content, structure, links and unsubscribe and address requirements, with the specific fixes. 1 credit per scan.

Credits cost $0.010 each at any volume, from $5, with no subscription. New accounts get 10 free credits, no card required.

## Help desk guides

Short how-to answers. Each is also available as Markdown at the same address plus .md. Search them all at https://trovarci.sh/guides?q=your+question

- [How to add a DMARC record](https://trovarci.sh/guides/add-dmarc-record): In your DNS settings, add a TXT record named _dmarc with the value v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:you@yourdomain.com. Keep p=none for two to four weeks while reports arrive, then change it to p=quarantine, and later to p=reject. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/add-dmarc-record.md
- [Daily sending limit exceeded: what it means and what to do](https://trovarci.sh/guides/daily-sending-limit-exceeded): Your email account has sent as much as it may in a day, so the provider refuses more until the limit resets, usually within 24 hours. Stop sending from that account, wait, and spread the rest of the campaign over more days or more accounts. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/daily-sending-limit-exceeded.md
- [What an email bounce means: hard and soft bounces](https://trovarci.sh/guides/email-bounce-meaning): A bounce is a reply saying your email wasn't delivered. Codes starting with 5 are hard bounces: the address doesn't exist or the server refused it for good, so remove it. Codes starting with 4 are soft bounces, such as a full mailbox or a busy server, so it may work later. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/email-bounce-meaning.md
- [Find why your emails go to spam: 4 checks in order](https://trovarci.sh/guides/find-why-emails-go-to-spam): First check your domain's setup and blocklists with the free Domain Checker. Then open one of your emails in Gmail, choose Show original, and look for SPF, DKIM and DMARC: PASS. Then check your list for dead addresses, and last, score the email itself. Fix the first check that fails. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/find-why-emails-go-to-spam.md
- [How to create a Gmail app password](https://trovarci.sh/guides/gmail-app-password): Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google account, then open myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, type a name for the app and press Create. Google shows a 16-character code once: paste it into your app as the password, without spaces. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/gmail-app-password.md
- [Gmail sending limits: how many emails a day](https://trovarci.sh/guides/gmail-sending-limits): A personal Gmail account can send to 500 people a day, and one email can have at most 500 recipients. Google Workspace allows 2,000 a day per user, or 500 on a free trial. Go over, and Gmail stops you sending for up to 24 hours. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/gmail-sending-limits.md
- [Gmail SMTP settings: server, port and password](https://trovarci.sh/guides/gmail-smtp-settings): Server smtp.gmail.com, port 587 with STARTTLS or 465 with SSL, your full Gmail address as the username, and an app password instead of your normal password. A personal account can send to 500 people a day, Google Workspace to about 2,000. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/gmail-smtp-settings.md
- [Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC for Google Workspace](https://trovarci.sh/guides/google-workspace-spf-dkim-dmarc): Add a TXT record v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all at @. Generate a DKIM key in the Admin console under Apps, Google Workspace, Gmail, Authenticate email, and add it as a TXT record at google._domainkey. Then add a DMARC record at _dmarc, starting with p=none. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/google-workspace-spf-dkim-dmarc.md
- [How to get your domain or server off a blocklist](https://trovarci.sh/guides/remove-from-blocklist): Check which list you're on with the free Domain Checker, fix what caused it, then use that list's own removal page. Spamhaus removal is free at check.spamhaus.org. SpamCop listings expire on their own 24 hours after the last report. Barracuda has a removal form, usually handled within 12 hours. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/remove-from-blocklist.md
- [How to verify an email list before sending](https://trovarci.sh/guides/verify-email-list-before-sending): Export your list as a CSV, upload it to the Email Verifier, then keep the valid addresses, remove the invalid ones and decide on the risky ones. Download the clean list and import it back into the tool you send from. It costs 1 cent per address. Markdown: https://trovarci.sh/guides/verify-email-list-before-sending.md

## Full explanations (blog)

- [How to send bulk email from Gmail without getting blocked](https://trovarci.sh/blog/send-bulk-email-from-gmail): Gmail's daily limits (500 personal, 2,000 Google Workspace), app password setup and SMTP settings, what to do when Gmail blocks sending, and how to reach a list bigger than one account allows.
- [Email deliverability in 2026](https://trovarci.sh/blog/email-deliverability-guide-2026): The four things that decide where email lands, the Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook rules for bulk senders, and what to do for each problem.
- [Why your emails go to spam](https://trovarci.sh/blog/why-emails-go-to-spam): Finds the cause by situation: everyone or some people, sudden or always, the setup, the list or the message.
- [How to set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC](https://trovarci.sh/blog/spf-dkim-dmarc-setup): Step-by-step setup for the three records that prove email is from your domain.
- [SPF PermError: the 10 DNS lookup limit](https://trovarci.sh/blog/spf-permerror-10-dns-lookups-fix): Why SPF breaks after 10 lookups, how to count them, and three fixes.
- [Email domain health check](https://trovarci.sh/blog/email-domain-health-check): What each domain check result means, which to fix first, and how to protect a domain that sends no email.
- [Is my domain blacklisted?](https://trovarci.sh/blog/domain-blacklisted-check-fix): How to check, what causes a listing, how to get removed, and whether subdomains are affected.
- [How to send bulk email without getting blacklisted](https://trovarci.sh/blog/send-bulk-email-without-blacklist): List quality, bounce and complaint limits, volume, and a pre-send checklist.
- [How to clean an email list before sending](https://trovarci.sh/blog/clean-email-list-before-sending): What each verification result means and what to do with it, including catch-all addresses.
- [Gmail Promotions tab](https://trovarci.sh/blog/gmail-promotions-tab-fix): Why emails land in Promotions and how to reach Primary more often.
- [How to check phone numbers before sending bulk SMS](https://trovarci.sh/blog/check-phone-numbers-before-bulk-sms): Formatting, landlines, and cleaning a list collected by hand.
- [What bulk email really costs](https://trovarci.sh/blog/bulk-email-cost): Per-contact, per-email, sending-service and owned-software pricing compared at three list sizes over three years.
